findings.subject: src/wave2/func_00179298.cpp:26-27
findings.summary: Make the C++ declaration of func_0017a968 agree with its shared definition. This new C++ unit still declares the C entry point as taking DisplayObject * and const AnimationTable *, while include/game/screen.h and the compiled C definition in src/wave2/func_0017a968.c require Widget * and const NameTable *. The opaque tags are unrelated, not aliases, so the integrator interface unification has left two incompatible signatures for the same C-linked function. This is hidden by the C++ waiver and by all pointers occupying the same ARM argument registers. In an isolated probe, importing the actual shared header with C linkage into the otherwise unchanged C++ source produces ARMCC error #338: more than one instance of overloaded func_0017a968 has C linkage. Use one correctly C-linked shared prototype and consistent pointee types/conversions through the local handle/context rather than privately redeclaring a different API.
findings.title: Make the C++ widget-call declaration match the shared interface

findings.subject: src/wave2/func_001791e0.c:7
findings.summary: Represent the counted text-pointer payload without an artificial one-element bound. The function accepts any index below the signed count at +0x28, but texts is declared with length 1. For count >= 2 and index == 1 the guard succeeds and the returned texts[1] reads outside the declared array, introducing undefined C behavior in the recovered source. The original caller func_0017775c loops its index over that same count, so this is a counted table, not a fixed-index-zero lookup. Use a flexible trailing member or an evidence-backed true bound. An isolated change from texts[1] to texts[] preserves the complete 28-byte MATCH, so the false bound is not needed for exactness.
findings.title: Use a flexible member for the counted text-pointer tail

findings.subject: src/wave2/func_001770cc.c:12
findings.summary: Allow the animation-pointer payload to contain the slots used by real callers. animations is declared with one element, but func_00161240 calls this function with index 1 at 0x001613f8 and 0x00161450 on the same owner used for index 0. Consequently owner->animations[index] performs an out-of-bounds C access on those normal call paths before the null check can help, even though the fixed compiler reproduces the original machine load. This is a source-layout artifact rather than an original algorithm bug. Replace the trailing one-element array with a flexible member or the recovered real bound. An isolated animations[] variant still MATCHes all 64 bytes.
findings.title: Model the indexed animation tail with a sufficient bound

qualifications: Re-derived all 51 required functions in 50 sequential canonical-unit tools/match.py invocations under profile game: every function reports MATCH. This covers 2376 new bytes plus 560 bytes in revised accepted functions, 2936 reviewed bytes total. Source and catalogue hashes in all canonical result records agree with prepare. Scratch counterfactual/probe results are separate and receive no credit.

Read docs/known-issues-c003-wave2.md first, then the required source/review/gate rules. Reviewed all 48 new source units, both revised accepted units and all shared interfaces independently of the integrator. The no-argument selection cutover and merged Command/CommandQueue/CommandSystem fields agree with their consuming original branches. F01 is the remaining C++ declaration/definition disagreement; the new C++ unit otherwise reproduces the original type-3/5/6 dispatch.

SlotList alignment experiment: the aligned control header is byte-identical to the prepared render_state.h (SHA-256 0b6262cd81881e6019087d0d3b6fe4fbb4b42ef99f41d06bfcb7088fb093e03e). Both private source copies are byte-identical to canonical func_00118074.c (SHA-256 9ec18c612ca95dbe009c81b3df3ceacadcd1257296b28ba7d73dad979b795b6b). Removing only the aligned(8) attribute changes the header hash to 534c2a2cbd7eadcf332b1ea02b03c65f390e28b03b1fa6d40f860a64b7179231; both variants MATCH the full 68 bytes. Each compiler dependency file names its corresponding private header. Thus aligned(8) is not required for this checkpoint match. No claim is made that the complete unrecovered SDK alignment contract has been established. Evidence is under probes/aligned/ and probes/unaligned/.

Source-layout counterfactuals under probes/flexible_text/ and probes/flexible_animation/ change only the false one-element trailing array to a flexible member and MATCH 28/64 bytes respectively. The shared-interface probe under probes/shared_cpp/ imports the real screen header with C linkage and is rejected with ARMCC error #338, while the canonical C++ unit independently MATCHes 256 bytes. These are source-validity checks, not claims of a changed current cartridge binary.

All seven prepared header hashes were independently checked and the header inventory contains no source-local headers. Shared Screen/WidgetSlot/NameTable, ItemPage/ItemPageSet, graphics state, render state, command state and selection declarations were read in full and checked against their exercised uses. Partial layouts and integrator-chosen names do not establish full SDK classes or native-port ABI, and they do not excuse F01-F03.

Direct catalogue v3 inspection finds all 51 reviewed owners ordinary functions totalling 2936 bytes, with no veneer or multi_entry credit. External secondary entries were inspected through their containing multi_entry owner when necessary; those original groups remain uncredited.

Read both prepared fresh-build receipts: 103 total credited functions / 5056 bytes, equal code.bin and stored ExeFS .code hashes, 93 units and no cache hits. The recorded 206-test suite result was not rerun. Inherited original-switch and invalid-screen behavior remains as published. Full original-armlink layout/unwind reconstruction, runtime behavior tests, Windows reproduction and lower RomFS IVFC traversal remain separate unproven properties. No tracked source/header was edited and no build/finalization retry was run.
